Anecdote

AN-ik-doht -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, AN. Careful: it is anecdote, not 'antidote' -- the cure for a poison. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anecdote is a short, entertaining story about a real incident.

Every long car trip ends with Uncle Ray's anecdote about the runaway shopping cart.

Worked Example

Amara's college-essay draft is all numbers: 'I tutored for 120 hours and helped 14 students.' Her older brother, home from college, reads it over her shoulder. 'Tell me about ONE of them.' So she writes three sentences about the evening Jonah, who hated math, taught HER a shortcut he had invented -- and suddenly the essay breathes.

The Jonah story is an anecdote: a short account of one real moment. Writers and speakers prize anecdotes because a single true story lands harder than a page of statistics -- but remember that anecdotes are only single cases; 'anecdotal evidence' is the phrase for stories doing a job that really needs data.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — story → vignette → anecdote

story vs. anecdote

story vs. anecdote: Story is the plainest word -- any account of events, true or invented, long or short.

vignette vs. anecdote

vignette vs. anecdote: Vignette is the strongest and most crafted: an anecdote is casually told for interest or laughs, but a vignette has been polished like a miniature painting, every detail placed on purpose.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of anecdote.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — an-

prefix — an-: not (Greek)

prefix — ek-

prefix — ek-: out (Greek)

root — dot-

root — dot-: given (Greek didonai 'to give')

Put it together

Put it together: Anecdote is Greek for 'things NOT given out' -- an- ('not') + ek- ('out') + dotos ('given'): the unpublished stories. The historian Procopius titled his secret, gossipy history of the emperor's court 'Anekdota' -- the tales too juicy to publish. An anecdote is still exactly that: the small true story that never makes the official record, told across a dinner table instead.

Use the root in a new word: antidote

Use the root in a new word: antidote: The ranger's kit carries an antidote for the canyon's one venomous snake.

Root Check

Word Choice

An anecdote is short, entertaining, and TRUE (or at least told as true) -- a real moment, not an invented plot. Speakers open with anecdotes, essays turn on them, and grandparents polish the same ones for decades. Two cautions: don't confuse it with antidote (the remedy for a poison -- the words differ by two letters), and treat 'anecdotal evidence' as a warning label: one good story is not the same as proof.
